language.label: Language
language.hint: The language of Sevak's windows and tray menu. Automatic follows your operating system. Plugin results stay in English for now.
language.reviewNote: Languages other than English are machine-drafted and await review by native speakers.

common.otherEntries: Other entries in the config file (not known to this list):
common.offUntilOn: Off until you turn it on.
common.pluginOff: “{name}” is switched off under Plugins. Switch it on there as well.

files.bufferSub: Collect several files from the results with Alt+Down, then move, copy, zip or trash them together.
files.keepBuffer: Keep the buffer when Sevak hides
files.keepBufferHint: Off empties the buffer every time the search bar closes.
files.keepBufferToggle: Keep the file buffer when Sevak hides
files.bookmarksSub: Search your browsers’ bookmarks. They are read from disk when you search; nothing is sent anywhere.
files.bookmarksKeywordHint: Type “keyword term” to search only bookmarks. Empty removes the keyword.
files.bookmarksGlobalHint: Also list matching bookmarks for plain searches.
files.browsersHint: Tick the browsers to read, with all their profiles. None ticked reads every browser Sevak finds. Safari exists on macOS only, and Sevak needs Full Disk Access there to read it.
files.recentSub: Type {keyword} to list the files you used lately, newest first, or {keyword} report to filter them by name.
files.recentEnabledHint: Off removes the search; nothing is read.
files.recentItemsHint: How many recent files the list holds (10 to 500).
files.recentPrivacy: Privacy: the list comes from the operating system’s own recent files (Linux recently-used.xbel, the Windows Recent folder, macOS Spotlight), read on this computer only. Network locations are skipped; nothing is sent anywhere.

clock.title: World clock
clock.sub: The time anywhere, offline: {keyword} lists your cities, {keyword} tokyo shows one place and {keyword} 3pm pst in ist converts a time, daylight saving time included. Enter copies the answer.
clock.citiesHint: What a bare keyword lists, after the time here: a city (San Francisco), an abbreviation (IST) or a time-zone name (Europe/Berlin).
clock.citiesEmpty: None added: only the time here is listed.

passwords.title: Password generator
passwords.sub: Random passwords made on this computer: {keyword}, {keyword} 24, {keyword} 6 words or {keyword} pin. Enter copies one, marked so that clipboard histories leave it out. Nothing generated is saved or logged.
passwords.symbolsHint: Add symbols such as !#%+ to passwords (letters and digits are always used).

ssh.title: SSH hosts
ssh.sub: Type {keyword} web to connect to a host from ~/.ssh/config in a terminal (the one chosen under Terminal commands).
ssh.knownHostsHint: Hosts you connected to before (from ~/.ssh/known_hosts). Hashed entries cannot be read and are skipped.
ssh.privacy: Privacy: only ~/.ssh/config, the files it includes inside ~/.ssh and (if on) known_hosts are read, never a private key. Nothing is sent anywhere; ssh runs only when you press Enter.

projects.title: Recent projects
projects.sub: Type {keyword} sevak to reopen a folder or workspace in the editor you last used it in.
projects.editorsHint: None ticked reads every editor that is installed.
projects.privacy: Privacy: the editors’ own recent lists are read from their settings folders and kept in memory only. Remote (SSH, WSL, container) and network-share projects are skipped.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.sub: Type {keyword} for today and the next days, {keyword} tomorrow or {keyword} fri. Events come from .ics files on this computer only: no accounts, no network.
calendar.filesHint: Export an .ics file from your calendar app, or point at a folder a sync tool fills (searched three levels deep).
calendar.pickFolder: Choose a folder of calendar files
calendar.daysHint: How far ahead the agenda looks.
calendar.privacy: Privacy: the files are read into memory when Sevak starts and on each refresh. Events are never written anywhere else, logged or sent, and are kept out of the search history.

tasks.title: Tasks & media
tasks.lead: Ready-made actions for the operating system, and the buttons of whatever is playing.
tasks.tasksSub: Dark mode, volume, screenshots, quit or kill an app, eject a drive, keep the computer awake and more. Type a task’s name, or {keyword} to list them all.
tasks.confirmHint: Confirm before force quitting an app, ending a process and restarting Explorer or Finder.
tasks.keywordHint: Type the keyword and a space to list the tasks. Empty removes the keyword.
tasks.globalHint: Also match task names in plain searches such as “dark mode” or “kill chrome”.
tasks.offerHint: Untick a task to hide it. Only the tasks that work on this computer are offered at all.
tasks.noteWindows: Toggling Wi-Fi or Bluetooth needs Settings, Privacy & security, Radios to allow desktop apps.
tasks.noteMac: The first use of dark mode, volume, quit or hide-others asks for permission to control System Events; hide-others and show-desktop also need Accessibility.
tasks.noteLinux: Tasks that need a helper program (wmctrl, nmcli, udisksctl…) are not listed when it is not installed.
tasks.mediaSub: Play, pause, next and previous for whatever is playing, without switching to the player: type pause or {keyword} .
tasks.mediaKeywordHint: Type the keyword and a space to list the buttons and the track. Empty removes the keyword.
tasks.mediaGlobalHint: Also match “pause”, “next track” and so on in plain searches.
tasks.mediaGlobalToggle: Show media controls in ordinary searches
tasks.nowPlayingHint: A row with the title, artist and app. It is read from your media player when you search, and never stored or sent anywhere.
tasks.mediaNoteLinux: Needs playerctl: the buttons and the track are not offered until it is installed.
tasks.mediaNoteMac: Buttons use the media keys. The playing track can only be read from Music and Spotify.
tasks.mediaNoteWindows: Uses the system media session (the one in the volume flyout), else the media keys.

system.title: System & terminal
system.lead: Lock, sleep, restart and shut down from the search bar, and run shell commands in a terminal.
system.commandsSub: Type a command’s name, such as lock or restart, or the name of a settings page, such as bluetooth.
system.confirmHint: Confirm before restart, shut down, log out and emptying the trash. This also applies to a hotkey bound to one of them.
system.offerHint: Untick a command or settings page to hide it. Only the ones that exist on this computer are offered at all.
system.noteMac: Restart, shut down, log out and emptying the Trash use System Events and need Accessibility permission for Sevak the first time.
system.noteLinux: Settings pages open through gnome-control-center, so they are offered on GNOME only.
system.terminalSub: Type > git status and press Enter to run it in a terminal window. Nothing runs until you press Enter.
system.terminalHint: A program name or full path, optionally with arguments, such as {example}. Empty detects one.
system.shellHint: The program that runs the command, such as {example}. Empty detects one.
system.shellHintMac: Not used on macOS: the terminal starts your login shell, so your aliases work.
system.keepOpenHint: Leave it at a shell prompt after the command exits. Off closes it when the command is done.
system.history: Recent commands are offered again from Sevak’s usage history, which stays on this computer.
system.historyWindows: Commands run without your shell’s profile, so aliases and functions are not available.
system.historyLinux: Commands run through the shell in non-interactive mode, so aliases from .bashrc are usually not available.

clipboard.title: Clipboard & paste
clipboard.lead: Clipboard history lets you type cb to paste something you copied earlier: text, images and files. Pasting options below also apply to snippets.
clipboard.keepHint: Off until you turn it on. Only what you copy after that is remembered.
clipboard.privacy: Privacy: while this is on, Sevak watches the clipboard and keeps what you copy on this computer, in its local data folder: text and the paths of copied files in clipboard-history.json, images as PNG files.
clipboard.encrypted: The files are encrypted for your Windows account.
clipboard.notEncryptedUnix: The files are not encrypted; they are readable only by your user.
clipboard.neverRecorded: Nothing is sent anywhere. Password managers and credential prompts are never recorded (see below).
clipboard.neverRecordedLinux: Nothing is sent anywhere. Password managers and credential prompts are never recorded (see below); on Linux a copy is skipped only when the app marks it as secret, so add other apps to Ignore apps.
clipboard.pluginOff: “Clipboard history” is switched off under Plugins, so cb shows nothing. Switch it on there as well.
clipboard.keepSub: These apply while the history is on.
clipboard.viewerRowsHint: Most entries listed at once. 5 to 100.
clipboard.previewCharsHint: Characters of an entry shown in its title. 40 to 500.
clipboard.itemsHint: Older entries are dropped, together with their image files.
clipboard.longestTextHint: Longer text is not recorded. 1 to {max} KB.
clipboard.encryptHint: Encrypts the history file and the images for your Windows account. Another user, another computer or a backup cannot read them.
clipboard.imagesHint: Copied pictures, saved as PNG files next to the history.
clipboard.largestImageHint: A picture whose PNG is bigger is not recorded. Up to {max} MB.
clipboard.filesHint: Copied files and folders: only their paths are kept; the files stay where they are.
clipboard.skipManagersHint: Never record copies made in KeePass, 1Password, Bitwarden and similar apps, or in system credential and passphrase prompts. Add other apps below.
clipboard.skipManagersToggle: Skip password managers and credential prompts
clipboard.ignoreHint: Copies made in these apps are never recorded, such as KeePassXC or 1Password. Program or app names, any case.
clipboard.clearHint: Deletes every saved entry and the image files. This cannot be undone.
clipboard.clearNote: This takes effect right away; it is not part of Save. You can also type cb clear in Sevak.
clipboard.restore: Put the clipboard back after pasting
clipboard.restoreHint: After pasting a clipboard entry or snippet, restore what was on the clipboard before. Off leaves the pasted text on it.
clipboard.pasteNoteMac: macOS pastes only with Accessibility permission for Sevak (System Settings, Privacy & Security). Without it, Sevak copies the entry instead.
clipboard.pasteNoteLinux: On Wayland, apps cannot be sent a paste, so Sevak copies the entry instead.
clipboard.pasteNoteWindows: Apps running as administrator cannot receive a paste; Sevak copies the entry instead.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.lead: Search your contacts and 1Password logins, and look up words. Contacts and 1Password are off until you turn them on; everything here stays on this computer.
integrations.contactsSub: Type {keyword} or @ and part of a name, address, number or company.
integrations.systemContactsMac: Also search the Contacts app. The first time you type the keyword, a row asks to allow access; until you do, only the vCard files below are searched.
integrations.systemContactsWindows: Also search the Windows People store. If your account’s contacts are not in it, export a vCard file instead.
integrations.systemContactsLinux: Also search Evolution's local address books. Other address books: export a vCard file.
integrations.vcardsHint: Export a .vcf file from your address book, Outlook, Google Contacts or a phone. A folder adds every .vcf in it. Works everywhere without a permission.
integrations.pickVcardFolder: Choose a folder of vCard files
integrations.contactPhotosHint: Use the photo in a vCard as the result icon. Photos stay in memory and are never written to disk.
integrations.contactsPrivacy: Privacy: contacts are read into memory when Sevak starts and every ten minutes. They are never written to disk, logged or sent anywhere, and searches here are kept out of the search history.
integrations.opSub: Find a login by title or website: {keyword} github. Sevak uses the official op command-line tool and never reads a password, a one-time code or a note.
integrations.opPathHint: Empty looks on PATH and in the usual install folders.
integrations.accountHint: Which account to use when several are signed in: its address (my.1password.com), short name or ID. Empty uses op’s default.
integrations.cacheHint: How long the list is kept in memory before it is refreshed. Refreshing may ask you to unlock 1Password.
integrations.opNeedsCli: Needs the 1Password CLI: install op and, in the 1Password app, turn on Settings, Developer, Integrate with 1Password CLI. op only runs when you type the keyword followed by a space.
integrations.opPrivacy: Privacy: Sevak asks op for the list of logins (titles, vault names, websites and usernames) and keeps it in memory only. What you search for here is kept out of the search history. op talks to 1Password as it normally does; Sevak sends nothing.
integrations.dictionarySub: Look up a word or fix its spelling, offline: {define} serendipity, {spell} recieve. Words you look up are not saved.
integrations.preferSystemMac: Use the macOS Dictionary for definitions. Off always uses the bundled English dictionary.
integrations.preferSystemWindows: Use the Windows spell checker for spelling. Off always uses the bundled English dictionary.
integrations.preferSystemLinux: Linux has no system dictionary Sevak can ask; it uses the bundled English dictionary and the word lists in /usr/share/hunspell. Off always uses the bundled English dictionary.

ai.title: AI assistant
ai.lead: Type {keyword} and a question in the launcher, press Enter and read (or copy, or paste) the answer. Off until you turn it on. Sevak never runs anything an answer says: it only shows it as text.
ai.notSent: Nothing is sent while you type, when Sevak starts, or in the background, and there is no telemetry. Questions and answers are kept in memory only: not logged, not written to disk, not in your search history.
ai.keywordHint: Type the keyword, a space, then your question.
ai.modelHint: Empty uses the default shown. Providers retire models, so type the name you want.
ai.baseUrlHint: Empty uses the default shown. Point the OpenAI-compatible provider at another server, such as http://localhost:1234/v1 for LM Studio.
ai.apiKeyHintRequired: Write-only: paste it and press Save key. It is never shown again.
ai.apiKeyHintOptional: Optional for a server on this computer. Write-only: paste it and press Save key.
ai.notAKey: That does not look like an API key (no spaces or line breaks).
ai.systemPromptHint: Sent with every question to set the tone. Keep secrets out of it: it goes to the provider too.
ai.longestHint: Asked of the model, in tokens ({min} to {max}). Roughly 0.75 words each. Longer answers cost more with paid services.
ai.timeoutHint: How long to wait for the whole answer ({min} to {max} seconds). A local model may need time to load.
ai.testHint: Checks the address, the key and the model with the values above (saved or not). It lists the provider's models and sends no question.
ai.keyKept: Where the key is kept: never in config.toml, never in a settings export or the diagnostics report, never in the log.
ai.envVars: The OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variables are used when no key is saved here. Press Save (below) to apply the other settings.

windows.title: Windows
windows.lead: Snap, resize and move the window you were using without touching the mouse, and jump to any open window by its title.
windows.enableHint: Turns the layouts and the window switcher on or off together.
windows.layoutsHint: Type the keyword and a space to list the layouts, then a layout such as left. Empty removes the keyword.
windows.switcherHint: Type the keyword and part of a window’s title or app to bring that window to the front. Empty turns the switcher off.
windows.gapHint: Space in pixels between snapped windows and the edge of the screen (0 to {max}). Scaled on high-DPI displays.
windows.globalHint: Also match layout names in plain searches such as “snap left” or “maximize”.
windows.noteWindows: Windows that run as administrator cannot be moved by Sevak unless Sevak runs as administrator too. The switcher lists the windows of the current virtual desktop.
windows.noteMac: Needs Accessibility access for Sevak (System Settings, Privacy & Security, Accessibility). The first use also asks to allow controlling System Events. Until both are granted, the keyword explains what is missing.
windows.noteLinux: Works in X11 sessions with a window manager that follows the EWMH standard. Wayland does not let applications move or list other windows, so there Sevak says so instead: use your desktop’s own tiling shortcuts, or log in to an X11 session.
windows.cheatSheetSub: The layouts act on the window you were in before Sevak opened. Type {layouts} to list them, or {switcher} and part of a title to switch.
windows.shortcutsNote: A layout can have a shortcut of its own: add a hotkey on the Hotkeys page that runs the result {run} (or windows:maximize, windows:next_display and so on; the name is the layout’s key). The shortcut acts on the window that has focus when you press it.

commands.almostMaximize: Fill most of the screen, with a margin
commands.center: Keep the size, center the window
commands.restore: Back to where the window was before

launcher.hotkeyUnavailable: Shortcut "{shortcut}" is unavailable: {error}. Choose another one in Settings (tray menu).

textView.label: Text
textView.truncated: The text is longer than what is shown.

destination.one: {count} item: type or browse to a folder.
destination.other: {count} items: type or browse to a folder.

ollama.label: Ollama (on this computer)
ollama.blurb: A model that runs on this computer. Nothing leaves it unless the base URL points elsewhere.

openai.label: OpenAI-compatible (ChatGPT, OpenRouter, LM Studio…)
openai.blurb: OpenAI, or any server that speaks the same API: change the base URL.

disclosure.local: When you press Enter on a question, Sevak sends the question you typed after “{keyword} ” (or the text you chose with “Ask AI about selection”), the system prompt below and the model name to {where}, which is this computer. Nothing leaves it.
disclosure.remote: When you press Enter on a question, Sevak sends the question you typed after “{keyword} ” (or the text you chose with “Ask AI about selection”), the system prompt below and the model name to {where}, over the internet. Nothing else is sent: not your clipboard, files or search history.

problems.wholeNumber: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}

baseUrl.scheme: The base URL must start with http:// or https://
baseUrl.spaces: The base URL cannot contain spaces
baseUrl.query: The base URL cannot contain a query or fragment
baseUrl.userInfo: The base URL cannot contain a user name or password
baseUrl.address: The base URL has an invalid address
baseUrl.noHost: The base URL needs a host name
baseUrl.host: The base URL has an invalid host name
baseUrl.port: The base URL has an invalid port

key.env: Using the {variable} environment variable. A key saved here would take its place.
key.envUnnamed: Using an environment variable. A key saved here would take its place.
key.unreadable: A saved key cannot be read (it was saved by another user or computer). Enter it again.
key.noneWithEnv: No key yet. Paste one here, or set the {variable} environment variable.

announce.largeType: Large Type: {text}. Press Escape to close.
announce.textView: Text view. Up and Down scroll, Escape goes back to the results.
announce.noResultsIndexing: No results yet, still indexing applications.

backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.lead: Save your settings, snippets, web searches, themes, script plugins and workflows to one file, and put them back on this or another computer. Nothing is sent anywhere.

settings.label: Settings
settings.description: Your shortcuts, appearance, search and plugin options, from config.toml. The 1Password section is left out.

snippets.label: Snippets
snippets.description: Your snippets and the snippet expansion options.

webSearch.label: Web search engines
webSearch.description: The web search engines and their keywords.

themes.label: Themes
themes.description: Theme files and your custom stylesheet.

plugins.label: Script plugins
plugins.description: Script plugins and the ones installed from the gallery, with their scripts. They run code, so Sevak asks you to allow each one again after a restore.

workflows.label: Workflows
workflows.description: Workflows and the ones installed from the gallery, with their scripts. Sevak asks you to allow each one that runs code again after a restore.

backUp.heading: Back up
backUp.leftOut: Left out of config.toml on purpose: {sections}.
backUp.plainFile: The backup is a plain file, not encrypted: anyone who can open it can read your snippets and scripts. Sevak makes it readable by you only; keep it somewhere you trust.
backUp.nowHint: “Back up now” saves to {folder} without asking.

restore.heading: Restore
restore.lead: Choose a backup file. Sevak checks it and shows what would change before it changes anything. A safety copy of what is replaced is saved first, so you can undo.
restore.restored: Restored. The new settings are already in use.
restore.undone: Undone. What the restore replaced is back.
restore.mergeHint: Adds what the backup has and overwrites what has the same name or setting. Keeps everything else you have.
restore.replaceHint: Makes the chosen categories exactly like the backup: what the backup does not have is removed, or goes back to its default.
restore.nothingInBackup: Nothing in the backup for this.
restore.scriptsNeverTrusted: Scripts are never trusted automatically. After the restore Sevak asks before it runs {names}. Which scripts you allowed is not part of a backup.
restore.allSame: Everything chosen is already the same: there is nothing to restore.

confirmReplace.one: Replace will remove {count} thing that is not in the backup (or reset it to the default). A safety copy is saved first, and “Undo restore” puts it back.
confirmReplace.other: Replace will remove {count} things that are not in the backup (or reset them to the default). A safety copy is saved first, and “Undo restore” puts it back.

restore.willAsk: Sevak will ask before it runs {names}.
restore.undoable: The last restore ({when}) can be undone. It puts back what was replaced: {categories}.

auto.heading: Automatic backups
auto.lead: Off unless you turn it on. Sevak keeps the newest few and deletes older automatic backups only; it never touches files you saved yourself.
auto.onUpdateToggle: Also back up when Sevak is updated
auto.folderHint: Used by automatic backups and “Back up now”. Leave empty for {folder}. A full path, or one starting with ~.
auto.cli: The same options are in backup.toml next to config.toml. From a terminal: sevak --backup <file>, sevak --restore <file>, sevak --undo-restore. In the launcher: backup settings, restore settings.

help.title: Help
help.lead: When something does not work, this report helps to find out why. Sevak has no telemetry, so it only exists here: it is made on this computer, nothing is sent anywhere, and you decide whether to share it. It holds the version, your system, which features are on, which plugins loaded and the last log lines. It does not hold what you searched for, your clipboard or snippets, the contents of scripts or workflows, contacts or passwords. Your user name, computer name and home folder are hidden. Read it before you paste it into a bug report at github.com/ninad-k/Sevak/issues/new/choose.
help.reportLabel: The report (read-only, exactly what is copied or saved)
help.copied: Copied to the clipboard. Paste it into your bug report.
help.cliHint: Without opening Settings: run sevak --diagnostics in a terminal. That report is made from files only, so it works even when Sevak is not running.

filters.heading: File search filters
filters.hint: Add these to f, ff or in searches, in any order. Every filter must match; - in front leaves out what follows.
filters.type: Also video, audio, doc, code, archive
filters.modified: Changed today, or in the last 7 days (>7d: longer ago)
filters.created: Created then, where the file system records it
filters.in: Inside that folder, or any folder of that name
filters.phrase: The name contains the exact phrase

marketplace.prompt: Want more, or made your own?

usage.title: Usage
usage.lead: What Sevak has counted on this computer to rank your results. Nothing leaves it.
usage.empty: Nothing counted yet. Launch something and it shows up here.
usage.privacy: Item names only: no typed searches, no folder paths. Copy stats copies the same text you see here.
usage.loadFailed: Could not read the usage statistics.

settings.title: Sevak Settings
settings.loadFailed: Could not load the settings. Close this window and try again from the tray menu.

general.shortcutWayland: Wayland: the desktop owns global shortcuts. Bind this key to sevak --toggle in your desktop settings, or let Sevak do it on GNOME.
general.shortcutHint: Shows and hides Sevak from anywhere.
general.notRegistered: This shortcut could not be registered: {error}
general.actionsHint: Acts on what you have selected in the app you are using: text, a link or files. Sevak copies the selection, shows what you can do with it and puts your clipboard back. Leave empty to turn it off.
general.actionsWayland: On Wayland, set it up with the button above (it binds sevak --actions).
general.acceptInjected: Accept shortcuts sent by other programs
general.acceptInjectedHint: Off: only keys you press count, so no other program can open Sevak by sending its shortcut. Turn on if AutoHotkey, PowerToys or another remapper types the shortcut for you.
general.clipboardFallback: Use the clipboard if the selection can't be read
general.clipboardFallbackHint: Wayland, terminal windows and apps Sevak may not control: act on what is on the clipboard instead.
general.primarySelectionHint: Universal Actions reads the PRIMARY selection, the text you have highlighted, before it presses Ctrl+C.
general.hideOnBlurHint: Closes the search bar when you click elsewhere.
general.updatesHint: Checks at startup, every six hours, and when opened if over an hour has passed. Asks before installing.
general.channelHint: Beta builds arrive earlier and may be less tested. Going back to Stable never downgrades: you get the next stable version.

startup.name: Start Sevak when I sign in
startup.hint: Start in the background for this account after sign-in. Your shortcut opens the launcher. Click Save to apply.
startup.windowsHint: Also managed in Windows Settings → Apps → Startup.
startup.macosHint: macOS can also restrict startup in System Settings → General → Login Items.
startup.linuxHint: Uses your desktop's autostart settings. Keep an AppImage in a permanent location.

state.otherCopy: Registered for another copy of Sevak

startup.needsEnableAgain: Your saved preference is on. Enable again restores startup for this account. This applies immediately and leaves other settings unchanged.
startup.needsRepair: Your saved preference is on. Repair startup registers this installed copy again. This applies immediately and leaves other settings unchanged.
startup.saveFirst: Save or undo your startup preference change before repairing.
startup.enabledMessage: Startup enabled. Sevak will start in the background after sign-in.
startup.changedOutsideOn: Your saved startup preference was changed outside Settings and is now on.
startup.changedOutsideOff: Your saved startup preference was changed outside Settings and is now off.
startup.previewStatus: Startup status is available in the installed app.
startup.previewRepair: Start Sevak to repair your account's startup setting.

search.maxResultsHint: How many rows the list shows.
search.fallbackHint: Offered when nothing else matches your query. config.toml can list several.
search.rememberHint: Up and Down on an empty search bar recall what you last ran. Kept on this computer only.

plugins.currencyHint: Calculator: “100 usd in eur”. Downloads the European Central Bank’s daily rates in the background, at most once a day. Off keeps Sevak offline.
plugins.expandHint: Typing a snippet’s keyword in any app replaces it with the snippet’s text. While this is on, Sevak watches your keystrokes for the keyword: the last few characters are kept in memory only, never saved, logged or sent anywhere, and ignored in Sevak’s own windows, terminals and password boxes it can detect. Needs a keyword on at least one [[snippet]]; not available on Wayland.
plugins.prefixHint: Typed before every keyword, such as ; so that ;sig expands and a plain sig does not. Empty expands bare keywords at the start of a word.
plugins.expandOnHint: Right away, or once a space or punctuation mark follows the keyword (which is kept).
plugins.immediate: As soon as it is typed
plugins.terminalsHint: Terminal windows are skipped unless this is on.
plugins.browsersHint: Off by default: a password field in a web page cannot be told from other text boxes, so a keyword typed inside a password would expand there.
plugins.ignoreAppsHint: Nothing is watched or expanded while one of these has focus, such as KeePassXC. Program or app names, any case.
plugins.note: Web search engines are edited under “Web search”. Changes apply when you save.

web.note: Type a keyword and your terms, such as g rust traits. {query} in the URL is replaced by what you type.
web.name: Name
web.empty: No engines. Web search is off until you add one.

files.foldersHint: Files and folders below these are searchable.
files.depthHint: How many levels below each folder are indexed.
files.networkHint: Windows: use \\server\share paths and mapped network drives. Off, Sevak never contacts them, because Windows signs in to a computer just from looking at its path.
files.keywordHint: Type “keyword name” to search only files. Add filters such as ext:pdf, size:>10mb or modified:7d (see Help).
files.globalHint: Also list matching files for plain searches, ranked lower.
files.wholeDiskHint: Type “{indexKeyword} name” to find files anywhere, or “{contentKeyword} words” to search inside them, through your computer’s own file index (Windows Search, Spotlight, locate or Tracker). Nothing leaves your computer.
files.sortHint: Relevance ranks by name match, Name sorts A to Z, Newest first shows recent changes first.
files.maxResultsHint: 0 uses the search limit under Search. Up to 50 here.

linux.xwaylandHint: Native Wayland windows cannot position themselves, so Sevak draws through XWayland to stay centered and typeable.

field.needsModifier: Hold Ctrl, Alt, Shift or Super together with the key.

list.note: Extra global shortcuts. A shortcut can open Sevak with text already typed in, such as g or > , or run a result directly without showing Sevak, using its result id such as apps:firefox.desktop.
list.noteWayland: On Wayland, run sevak --setup-hotkey (or use the button under General) after saving to bind them in GNOME.

validate.sameAsActions: Same as the Universal Actions shortcut
validate.fontFamily: Only letters, digits, spaces and , . _ - are allowed
validate.insideConfig: Must be a path inside the config folder
validate.urlScheme: Must start with http:// or https://
validate.size: Enter a size above 0, up to {max}

page.title: Workflows
page.lead: A workflow chains a trigger (a keyword, a shortcut, Universal Actions or a command) to actions and outputs. Build one here, or drop a folder with a workflow.toml into the workflows folder. A workflow that runs scripts or commands asks for your permission first.
page.empty: No workflows yet. Start with a template, or press New workflow. They live in {folder}.

editor.canvas: Workflow canvas. Boxes are nodes; drag from a dot on the right edge of a box to another box to connect them.
editor.portTitle: Drag to another box to connect ({port})
editor.needsApproval: This runs code or commands, so Sevak asks you to allow the workflow first.

hotkey.summary: A global shortcut starts the workflow.

key.label: Shortcut
key.hint: Like the shortcuts in Settings. On Wayland use an external trigger instead.

selection.summary: Appears in Universal Actions for the text, links or files you select.

accepts.label: Offer it for

external.label: External trigger
external.summary: Started from the command line or a desktop shortcut.

script_filter.label: Script filter
script_filter.summary: A keyword whose results come from a script (Alfred Script Filter JSON).

run_script.label: Run script
run_script.summary: Runs a program; what it prints becomes the argument.

log_stderr.label: Log its error output
log_stderr.hint: Off by default: it can contain your data.

open_url.label: Open URL
open_url.summary: Opens a web or mail link. Placeholders are URL-encoded.

url.label: Link
url.hint: Add |raw to a placeholder to leave it as it is: {var:site|raw}.

open_file.label: Open file
open_file.summary: Opens a file or folder with its default program.

path.label: Path
path.hint: ~ is your home folder; a relative path is inside the workflow's folder. Placeholders: {query} and {var:name}.

launch_app.label: Launch app
launch_app.summary: Starts an application by name or path.

args.label: Arguments
args.hint: Used when the application is a path to a program.

system_command.label: System command
system_command.summary: Lock, sleep, restart and so on.

terminal_command.label: Terminal command
terminal_command.summary: Runs a command line in a terminal window.

command.label: Command line
command.hint: Placeholders: {query} and {var:name}. Each one is inserted as one quoted word for your shell; {query|raw} inserts it as commands.

paste.label: Paste
paste.summary: Pastes text into the app you were using.

set_variable.label: Set variable
set_variable.summary: Stores a value for the nodes after it.

transform.label: Transform
transform.summary: Changes the argument, or stores the result in a variable.

find.hint: For replace, regular-expression replace and split.

into.label: Store in variable

delay.label: Delay
delay.summary: Waits a moment (at most a minute).

text_view.label: Text view
text_view.summary: Shows text in the launcher window.

markdown.label: Markdown
markdown.hint: Draw the text as Markdown: headings, lists, tables, links.

gallery.title: Gallery
gallery.lead: Add tools to your launcher with ready-made extensions and workflows. Choose Load gallery to browse packages from GitHub and check signed revocation notices, then install what you need. Script plugins ask for your permission before running. Themes are in Appearance → Theme editor.
gallery.fetches: Fetches the list and signed notices from GitHub.

skipped.other: {count} left out (not understood by this Sevak)

extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.lead: Workflows, script plugins, native extensions and themes from the Sevak gallery. Nothing is requested while you browse Settings: Load fetches the list once from the Sevak repository on GitHub and verifies signed revocation notices, and Install downloads that one package, checks it against the checksum in the list and puts it in your folder. Whatever you install is new and not allowed: Sevak asks for your permission before anything in it runs. No other data is sent.
extensions.statusUnknown: Current revocation status is unknown. Load or refresh the list to check signed extension advisories.
extensions.installedTheme: Installed the theme {name}. Choose it in Settings > Appearance.
extensions.installedItem: Installed {name}. It does not run until you allow it, if it can run code: Sevak asks next.
extensions.updated: Updated {name}. Sevak asks again if it can run code.
extensions.signedIndexTitle: The list's release signature was checked with Sevak's release key before it was read.

permission.network: connects to the internet or your network
permission.filesystem: reads or writes files outside its own folders
permission.clipboard: reads or changes the clipboard itself

warning.native: A native extension is a compiled program, not a script you can read. Sevak does not sandbox it: once you allow it, it runs with your account's permissions. It never runs before you allow it in the dialog that follows, which shows its publisher, the permissions it declares and its checksum.
warning.theme: A theme only changes colors and sizes. It is checked and rewritten before it is saved.
warning.plugin: A script plugin runs code. It does not run until you allow it in the dialog that follows.
warning.workflow: A workflow that runs a program or pastes into another app waits for your permission; one that only opens links does not run any code.
